title: Choose the visual world for DevLens
question: The roll assigned Transit Line. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. It applies to /replay first, then home and /record.

options.label: Transit Line
options.thesis: The session is a line you ride: stations are events, the fail-to-pass route is the one coloured line.
options.viewport: Top: the take drawn as a line diagram with red failed-test stations, green terminus, amber sandbox line at the interchange. Below: video left, the selected station's evidence (diff, test, question, verbatim answer) right; unknowns strip always visible.
options.risk: If the line is decoration instead of the click target, it reads as an infographic, not a tool.

raised.raise: One reserved course colour rides over the evidence and never edits it: the fail-to-pass route.
Nothing disappears, it cancels: the superseded patch stays on the line, stamped superseded.
Provenance is a layer: observed evidence is the ground, rule links and developer words sit on labelled layers above it.
Selecting a station focuses its corridor while the rest of the network stays readable.
Hierarchy by scale contrast, not by boxes and cards.

options.label: Annotated Paper
options.lineage: scholarly citation apparatus: superscripts, footnotes, margin notes
options.thesis: Every sentence on the page is a claim, and every claim carries its citation to an event.
options.viewport: A numbered list of claims in a reading column, superscript event ids opening margin notes with the raw event; the video sits in the right margin.
options.risk: Closest to the editorial-hairline look many AI builds land on; familiar and calm, less memorable.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.thesis: Each claim sits beside the interface detail that proves it.
options.viewport: Alternating rows: a one-line claim, then its proof panel (test output, diff, re-run).
options.case: Strong product clarity; weak audience identification, it reads as marketing.
options.risk: Can look like a landing page instead of a working review screen.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A course rides in purple over fixed terrain.
options.viewport: Map terrain with a purple course.
options.risk: Reviewers do not read maps to review code.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the route that never edits the ground.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: One leg per coupon; void stamps cancel, never delete.
options.risk: Nostalgia costume on a work screen.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Leaves on plies above a coloured board.
options.risk: Heavy material for a few-minute review.

options.label: Midnight Transit Mural
options.thesis: The same line world on midnight-blue enamel.
options.risk: Drifts toward the dark neon AI look you ruled out.
options.case: Near-duplicate of the roll; loses on your 'no generic AI look' constraint.
options.kept: Focus the chosen corridor, keep transfer context.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-tool review page, like a pull request with CI checks.
canonCard.viewport: Header, checks list, video and diff in tabs, questions in a sidebar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any dev tool by design.
